notes: Wisdom, skill, or insight. In Greek culture it meant philosophy and clever speech, and in Jewish writings it often meant practical, God-given insight for living well. elsewhere.note: Wisdom speaks about her place in creation.
In Christ are hidden all the treasures of wisdom.

range.note: What the cross looks like to the world.

elsewhere.note: The natural person finds God's things foolishness.
The wisdom of this world is foolishness with God.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

elsewhere.note: We boast in sufferings.

A division among them over Jesus.

Boast only in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ.

elsewhere.note: It is sown a natural body; it is raised a spiritual body.

My defense to those who examine me.

Epaphroditus, my brother and fellow worker.
Titus is my partner and fellow worker.

The testing of your faith, more precious than gold.

A little yeast leavens the whole lump.

In Antioch there were prophets and teachers.
A great prophet has arisen among us.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Something set aside for destruction or under a curse, from "set up" or "devoted." In 12:3 no one speaking by the Spirit can say "Jesus is anathema" (accursed), and in 16:22 Paul says that anyone who does not love the Lord is "accursed."

elsewhere.note: I would wish to be accursed and cut off from Christ.
Let him be accursed.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: to be patient, to be slow to anger
notes: Literally "long-tempered" (makros "long" plus thymos "anger or passion"), the opposite of a short temper. It is the first thing Paul says about love (13:4). The same word describes God's patience with people.

elsewhere.note: Have patience with me.
The Lord is patient with you.
Be patient until the coming of the Lord.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To show kindness, to act in a useful and gracious way. It appears only here in the New Testament, as the second line about love (13:4). It belongs to the same family as chrēstotēs, "kindness."

elsewhere.note: Love is patient and kind.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: to be jealous, to be eager
notes: To be zealous or eager, which can be good (eager for good gifts, 12:31; 14:1) or bad (jealous or envious, 13:4). Context decides. It is related to zēlos, "zeal, jealousy."

elsewhere.note: The patriarchs, becoming jealous of Joseph, sold him.
They zealously seek you, but not for good.
You covet and cannot obtain.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: to brag, to be a windbag
notes: To boast or show off. It is found only here in the New Testament, in the line "Love doesn't brag" (13:4), and the root suggests puffing oneself up with empty talk.

elsewhere.note: Love doesn't brag, is not proud.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

range.note: What God gives to be said.

elsewhere.note: If prophecy, let's prophesy according to the proportion of our faith.
Don't despise prophecies.
Blessed is he who reads the words of the prophecy.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A mirror, in Paul's day made of polished metal (Corinth was famous for its bronze), which gave only a blurry image. In 13:12, "now we see in a mirror dimly" describes how limited our present knowledge is.

elsewhere.note: Like a man looking at his natural face in a mirror.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

elsewhere.note: Now we see in a mirror dimly.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: An intensified form of ginōskō, "to know," meaning to know fully or to recognize. In 13:12, Paul says that one day "I will know fully, even as I was fully known."

elsewhere.note: Their eyes were kept from recognizing him.
Knowing the ordinance of God.
Understood the grace of God in truth.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Disorder, unrest, confusion. In 14:33, "God is not a God of confusion, but of peace." The word was also used of civil unrest and disturbances.

elsewhere.note: When you hear of wars and tumults.
Where jealousy and selfish ambition are, there is confusion.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

elsewhere.note: They were unlearned and ordinary men.
Even if I am unskilled in speech.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

elsewhere.note: In the order of his division.
Rejoicing to see your order.
A priest forever after the order of Melchizedek.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A word borrowed from Hebrew meaning "so be it" or "truly." Congregations said it in agreement at the end of prayers (14:16), and Paul uses it to close the letter (16:24).

elsewhere.note: Who is blessed forever. Amen.
For yours is the kingdom, the power, and the glory forever. Amen.
Yes, come, Lord Jesus.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To take from someone, so to receive what has been handed on. Paul uses it with paradidōmi ("hand over") for the passing on of the gospel and of the Lord's Supper: "what I also received" (11:23; 15:1, 15:3).

elsewhere.note: If anyone preaches to you any gospel other than what you received.
The things which you learned and received and heard and saw in me.
I will come again and will receive you to myself.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Dead, whether a dead body or a dead person. In chapter 15 it is used constantly for "the dead," in the phrase "the resurrection of the dead," and for Christ's being "raised from the dead."

elsewhere.note: As Christ was raised from the dead.
He is not the God of the dead, but of the living.
The firstborn from the dead.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: The first part of a harvest, offered to God as a promise of the rest. Paul says Christ is "the firstfruits of those who are asleep" (15:20, 15:23), meaning his resurrection is the first of a larger harvest. Stephanas's household were the "firstfruits of Achaia" (16:15).

elsewhere.note: We ourselves have the first fruits of the Spirit.
Epaenetus, the first fruits of Asia.
That we should be a kind of first fruits of his creatures.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: to abolish, to bring to nothing
notes: To make ineffective or to put out of action (kata, "down," plus argos, "idle"). In chapter 15 it describes how Christ will "abolish" every rule and authority and power, and the last enemy, death (15:24-26).

elsewhere.note: Do we then nullify the law through faith?
Our Savior Christ Jesus, who abolished death.
That through death he might destroy him who had the power of death.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

elsewhere.note: Delivered from the bondage of corruption.
He who sows to his own flesh will reap corruption.
Having escaped from the corruption that is in the world.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

elsewhere.note: To those who by patience in well-doing seek for immortality.
Brought life and immortality to light.
Grace be with all those who love our Lord Jesus Christ with incorruptible love.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Deathlessness (a- "not" plus thanatos "death"). In 15:53-54 Paul says "this mortal must put on immortality." In the New Testament, immortality is something God gives, not something people have by nature (see 1 Timothy 6:16).

elsewhere.note: He alone has immortality.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

elsewhere.note: In a moment, in the twinkling of an eye.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

elsewhere.note: Until he leads justice to victory.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

elsewhere.note: Now concerning the collection for the saints.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: to act like a man, to be brave
notes: To be courageous (from anēr, "man"). In 16:13 it is one of a series of short commands to the whole church, "Watch, stand firm in the faith, be courageous, be strong."

elsewhere.note: Be courageous, be strong.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: to be strong, to be strengthened
notes: To become strong or to be made strong. In 16:13, "be strong," the last of a group of commands. The verb is passive in form, suggesting strength is received.

elsewhere.note: The child grew and became strong in spirit.
To be strengthened with power through his Spirit.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

elsewhere.note: Out of her poverty she put in all that she had.
Your abundance at this present time supplies their lack.
To supply what was lacking in your service toward me.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

elsewhere.note: You gave me no kiss.
Judas, do you betray the Son of Man with a kiss?
Greet one another with a kiss of love.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

The message about Jesus, later also a name for books like Mark.

elsewhere.note: The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ.
The gospel I preached to you.
The gospel that was preached by me.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

elsewhere.note: The Sadducees say there is no resurrection.
I am the resurrection and the life.
How can some of you say there is no resurrection?
This is the first resurrection.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

elsewhere.note: "He is risen, as he said."
"The Lord is risen indeed."
Believe that God raised him.
He was raised on the third day.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

elsewhere.note: Many bodies of the saints who had fallen asleep were raised.
Some have fallen asleep.
Those who are asleep.

The Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world.
If we confess our sins.

elsewhere.note: O death, where is your sting?
Tails like scorpions, with stings.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

elsewhere.note: The Word was full of grace and truth.
The gospel of the grace of God.
By grace you are saved.

range.note: A title of honor for those who serve the Lord.

elsewhere.note: Whoever wishes to be first among you must be your slave.

Taking the form of a servant.

elsewhere.note: "Peace to you."
My peace I give to you.
The peace of God that surpasses understanding.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

elsewhere.note: The circumcision party criticized Peter.

We are the circumcision, who worship by the Spirit of God.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

elsewhere.note: Jesus comes to John to be baptized.
Jesus is baptized in the Jordan.
Be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ.

range.note: In the Psalms, God as a rock and refuge.

elsewhere.note: The wise builder on the rock.
"The rock was Christ."
A rock that makes people fall.
A rock of offense.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

elsewhere.note: Do not lead us into temptation.
No temptation has taken you but such as is common.
Count it all joy when you meet trials.
The Lord knows how to rescue the godly from trials.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

elsewhere.note: The fellowship.
The favor of taking part in the relief of the saints.
Your partnership in the gospel.

He broke the loaves.
He took bread, broke it, and gave it.
The Lord Jesus took bread.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

elsewhere.note: I have lived before God in all good conscience.
Their conscience, being weak, is defiled.
From a pure heart and a good conscience.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

elsewhere.note: They saw his glory.
The light of the knowledge of the glory of God.
He is the radiance of God's glory.

Life, the breath of a person.

elsewhere.note: The Holy Spirit will come on you.
Receive the Holy Spirit.
The fruit of the Spirit.

Whoever has a gift of service.
The ministry of reconciliation.

elsewhere.note: They will speak in new tongues.
Various kinds of tongues.

Persons from every tribe and language.

The twelve, and later others such as Paul.

elsewhere.note: Whom he also named apostles.
Numbered with the eleven apostles.
Then to all the apostles.

elsewhere.note: "Not everyone who says to me, 'Lord, Lord.'"
God has made him both Lord and Christ.
Every tongue will confess that Jesus Christ is Lord.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

He who sanctifies and those who are sanctified.
In your hearts, honor Christ as Lord.

Justified by his grace.

They will give account to him who is ready to judge.

Those he justified he also glorified.

Without flaw, in the older English sense.

Wisdom among the mature.

Being trustworthy and loyal (STEPBible tags this sense separately).

Delivered from the power of darkness.

If there is any encouragement in Christ.

The church, which is his body.
